title: Apply Operations to Make Two Strings Equal
summary: Given two binary strings s1 and s2 of the same length n , and a positive integer x , determine the minimum cost required to make s1 equal to s2 by flipping characters.
statement: Given two binary strings s1 and s2 of the same length n , and a positive integer x , determine the minimum cost required to make s1 equal to s2 by flipping characters. Flipping any two non-adjacent characters in s1 costs x , while flipping adjacent characters costs 1. Return -1 if it is impossible to make the strings equal.
constraints: One operation flips any two positions for cost x or two adjacent positions for cost one.
Return the minimum cost to transform s1 into s2, or -1 when impossible.
hints: Only mismatch positions matter, and they must be paired.
In sorted mismatch order, an optimal plan pairs the two ends arbitrarily or adjacent positions locally.
Memoize an interval and try outer arbitrary flip, left adjacent pair, or right adjacent pair.
Uncrossing shows a cheapest pairing has one of these forms, so the interval recurrence covers an optimum.
editorial: Uncrossing shows a cheapest pairing has one of these forms, so the interval recurrence covers an optimum.

tests.explanation: Pairing mismatch positions by cheap adjacent moves or cost-two arbitrary flips gives minimum four.
The mismatch pairing dynamic program gives the minimum valid transformation cost.
